CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male who presents with complaints of shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. He reports noticing leg swelling and feeling lethargic. Dyspnea is exertional, occurring with exertion such as walking up a flight of stairs. He denies dyspnea at rest while sitting. He reports some discomfort lying flat in bed and morning stiffness that takes time to resolve. He endorses one episode of acute nocturnal dyspnea approximately one week ago that has not recurred. Patient attributes symptoms to dietary indiscretion including consumption of salty foods at social gatherings. Regarding his diabetes, patient reports good blood sugar control during the working week with consistent monitoring, though monitoring is less consistent on weekends. He denies recent blood sugar spikes. Regarding his depression, patient reports it has been a challenging year and a half. He attempted natural solutions including outdoor stretches in the summer but is seeking alternatives as weather has changed. He is not yet ready to try medications but is open to suggestions. Regarding his reflux, patient is on omeprazole and has been making lifestyle modifications including reducing Red Bull and caffeine intake. Alcohol intake has been reduced, particularly after a difficult holiday season. Patient denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Endorses shortness of breath. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type I diabetes
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys chocolate bars. Monitors blood glucose during work week but less consistently on weekends. Previously engaged in outdoor stretches for depression management. Alcohol consumption reduced but remains challenging during holidays. Has been reducing caffeine and Red Bull intake as part of reflux management.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Stable with good oxygen saturation
Neck: No jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits
Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated
Pulmonary: Crackles bilaterally at bases
Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in lower extremities

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease or pneumonia
Laboratory studies: Normal white blood cell count, no signs of infection

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute congestive heart failure exacerbation: Start Lasix 40 mg daily. Patient to weigh himself daily and call if weight does not decrease or if weight increases. Patient instructed to call or go to emergency room if shortness of breath worsens at rest, as may require intravenous diuretics.

2. Type I diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c in approximately one month to assess need for adjustments. Patient to follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam completed.

3. Depression: Referral to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications initiated at this time.

4. Reflux: Continue omeprazole 20 mg daily.
